answer: Latency Shadow Registry.** Each agent gets a randomly assigned relay path whose timing signature is recorded at registration. Duplicate identities, even with fresh keys, inherit near-identical latency profiles from the same host, so the registry flags correlated shadows like a nebula of matching delays. An attacker must forge genuinely distinct network paths per identity, leasing separate hosts and routes, which multiplies infrastructure cost per fake agent far beyond the velvet cost of one key. Registration is free; passing shadow checks is not.
